links.outcome: Calibration (log loss, over-prediction) versus discrimination (AUROC/AUPRC) after class imbalance correction
links.effect: Correction methods did not improve AUROC or AUPRC but severely compromised calibration, with risk over-prediction up to 62.8% and increased log loss across all mitigation techniques.
links.quote: However, these methods severely compromised model calibration, leading to significant over-prediction of risks (up to a 62.8 % increase) as further evidenced by increased log loss across all mitigation techniques.

unlisted_practices: Avoid class imbalance correction (oversampling, SMOTE, undersampling, cost-sensitive learning) when developing clinical prediction models that need calibrated risks

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation on >1.8M patients investigating the safety and calibration impact of class imbalance correction techniques (oversampling, undersampling, cost-sensitive learning) on simulated clinical decision making.

primary.practice: class imbalance correction during model development/validation
